$comment: Machine-verifiable claims in docs/ and what checks each. Read by scripts/check-docs-drift.ts (pnpm check:docs-drift). The rules block is the contract; an entry that does not fit it is a manifest error, not a skipped check.

evaluation.live: Checked against the current checkout and the live GitHub API. A failure is drift. Used for the two indexes (docs/adr/README.md, docs/plans/README.md), the runbooks, the Status and Date of every record, the Decision of a record that is still Accepted or Accepted (corrected ...), the standing part of a record superseded only in part, and plans the plans index does not mark Shipped.
evaluation.historical: A claim that describes the world as it stood when it was written, which ADR 0012 forbids correcting once overtaken: the Context, Consequences, Alternatives and Corrections of any record, every part of a superseded record, and every Shipped plan. It is checked at asOf, the commit that wrote the line (from git blame) or, for a citation of lines a squash-merged plan went on to modify, that commit's parent. So a claim that was already false when written is still drift, and one that was true then and has been overtaken since is not. A historical gh-api claim cannot be replayed, because the API keeps no history of settings; it is checked through the record chain instead: the record stating it must carry the status Superseded by ADR-<supersededBy>, and that record must exist.

methods.gh-api: check {endpoint, jq, equals}: `gh api <endpoint> --jq '(<jq>) | tojson'` must equal `equals`. {repo} expands to repository. Retried on HTTP 5xx, HTTP 429, a timeout or a network failure that got no HTTP status; still failing, or any other error, is `unrunnable`, never `pass`.
methods.file-line: check {path, line?, lineEnd?, contains | matches | absent, exists?}: the file (at asOf for historical) exists, and the line span, or the whole file without `line`, contains the text, matches the regex, or lacks the text. `exists: false` asserts the path is gone.
methods.config-value: check {file, json | regex | text, equals | equalsAll}: a JSON path, the first capture group of a multiline regex (all of them with equalsAll), or the trimmed file equals the claimed value.
methods.command: check {package, script, runs?}: the package.json scripts of `package` (at asOf for historical) define `script`, and it runs `runs` when given.

requires.admin: Reading branch protection and the repository's merge settings needs administration read. CI's GITHUB_TOKEN has none, so the workflow passes --skip-requires admin and those entries are reported as skipped, never as holding. The owner's token checks them locally. Any other token gets an error from the protection endpoint or a null for a merge setting, which GitHub leaves out of the response, and the entry is reported as could not run (exit 2), never as drift.

rules.anchors: Every entry names an exact substring of its doc. The checker resolves the line from it, so edits elsewhere in the doc do not break the entry; an anchor that has disappeared is `stale` (exit 1) until the entry is updated or removed.

coverage.rule: These tokens found under the roots must be covered by an entry's `covers`, or they are reported `uncatalogued` (exit 1): every relative Markdown link (inline, with a title, in angle brackets, or a reference definition); every backticked `pnpm` command outside fenced code blocks that runs a package script, in the forms the checker recognises (leading NAME=value assignments, --filter <pkg>, --filter=<pkg>, -F <pkg>, -r or --recursive, run <script>; pnpm's own subcommands excluded); and every path:line citation of a file with a .ts, .tsx, .mjs, .cjs, .js, .json, .yml, .yaml, .md, .css or .sh extension, directories starting with a dot included. Other forms, such as a citation of an extensionless file like .husky/pre-commit:3, are not recognised, so the manifest catalogues the claims of these kinds that the checker can find, not every claim a doc makes.

exclusions: Reasoning, trade-offs and recommendations: not true-or-false by machine.

Measurements taken at a date (Lighthouse and axe scores, contrast ratios, trace timings, bundle sizes, build durations, counts such as '74 accent text usages'): reproducing them needs a browser, a build or a specific machine state, and ADR 0012 treats them as history.
External facts (pnpm, Vercel, GitHub and Next.js behaviour, release notes, vendor statements, Cloudflare figures): outside the repository, verified by the review that wrote them.
Vercel project settings and deployment logs cited in the runbook and ADRs 0002, 0005, 0016: need the Vercel CLI and the owner's Vercel token, which CI does not have.

DNS records and HTTP response headers of the live site (runbook, ADR 0005): network state that changes independently of the repository; the runbook's own verification commands check them at deploy time.

Dated observations of live settings in records that are not superseded (for example ADR 0018's 'automated security updates are off when this record is accepted'): the API keeps no history to replay them and no record chain supersedes them.
Self-citations such as '`## Consequences` at `:108`' inside a record: they point into the same file at the commit that wrote them and are not path:line tokens.
External URLs: link rot on third-party sites is not repository drift.
Shipped plans beyond their links, script names and citations: the plans index says shipped plans are kept as history, so their prose is not re-verified.
